title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-08 16:00 PDT | Duration 45m | Recording available
Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel (Redwood) — Aisha Khan, Diego Martinez, Priya Rao, Liam O'Connor (Nexa)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Aisha: Hey Maya, here. Diego here. Priya here. Liam joining now.
[00:14] Samir: Great, thanks. Agenda is the usual — onboarding, results from last week's bench, security checklist, and next steps.
[00:22] Aisha: Sounds good. Diego you took the lead on infra access last week, any updates?
[00:28] Diego: Yeah, we spun up the test VPC and tried the peering, hit a couple of route issues. We have the firewall rules open but, um, the egress NAT wasn't configured so some requests timed out.
[00:40] Maya: Ok that matches what we saw — some incomplete handshakes on the initial TLS. If you can add the NAT gateway for the subnet we'll have steady egress. Also we need the service account with compute and network viewer roles so Redwood can initiate the peering tests.
[00:55] Diego: Yep, will do. I'll share the account details after this call.
[00:59] Priya: Quick security note — we need confirmation about KMS key usage. Are keys customer-managed in the private deployment?
[01:07] Samir: Yes, in Redwood Private customers can bring-your-own KMS keys. For the hosted POC we used Redwood-managed keys but for the VPC/private run we can wire up your KMS, there's a short integration doc. I'll send it.
[01:19] Aisha: Great. On the bench results, Liam can you summarize?
[01:23] Liam: Sure — we ran the default model variant on a 2k context, did 3 runs with mixed payloads. Average p99 latency is around 420ms, cost per 1k tokens was about $0.38 in our test (not accounting for batching). We did notice token inflation on longer prompts — so prompt trimming helps.
[01:40] Samir: Hmm, 420 p99 is a bit higher than expected for that config. Can you share the raw traces? Were you using continuous batching or single-call?
[01:49] Liam: Single-call, we didn't enable batching. We can re-run with Redwood's recommended batching profile.
[01:54] Maya: That's a good call — our baseline for similar payloads with batching is usually around 280–320ms p99 on Dedicated-ish setups. Also KV cache wasn't enabled in your config — that can cut repeated prefix token costs a lot.
[02:08] Diego: KV cache — we thought that was only for certain models?
[02:12] Samir: It's broadly available but behaves slightly differently by architecture. We'll include concrete steps in the how-to doc.
[02:19] Aisha: For the POC success criteria, we said p99 under 350ms and cost per 1k under $0.30, right?
[02:26] Maya: Yes those were the target numbers from the deck. We're flexible if we can show a roadmap (e.g., enable batching + quantization = meet targets).
[02:35] Liam: About quantization, we tried an 8-bit variant and saw quality drift on some summarization prompts. Any recommendations?
[02:43] Samir: Quality vs cost — for summarization we recommend the 6/8 mixed scheme only after a brief eval set. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per workload, we can run a small quality regression on your eval set.
[02:56] Priya: Also need to know about audit logs and retention for the private deployment. Should logs be pushed to our SIEM?
[03:03] Samir: Yes, audit logs can stream to your SIEM. We support S3, Kafka, and direct push. Retention policy is configurable — we can provide defaults and update to match your compliance.
[03:15] Aisha: Can you go over the bench configs you'll run this week?
[03:18] Maya: We'll run two canonical configs: (1) baseline single-call with current model and no batching (to compare apples-to-apples), (2) optimized: batching enabled, KV cache on, and quant suggestion (if quality ok). We'll share raw traces and a summarized sheet.
[03:33] Diego: For the optimized run — will that require changes to our VPC settings?
[03:38] Samir: Only minor — persistent connections are preferred and opening long-lived sockets is helpful. Our agent will keep an outbound connection and we recommend increasing idle timeout on LB.
[03:49] Liam: One oddity — we saw occasional token duplication around 1% of calls; maybe a retry pattern on client side. Could that be client retries?
[03:58] Samir: Yes that often looks like a client-side retry without idempotency keys. We'll check traces to confirm. If it's retries we can suggest idempotency headers.
[04:08] Aisha: Any blockers on the security checklist? Priya?
[04:11] Priya: A few — we need the SOC2 artifact, a short note on key rotation for KMS, and confirmation that Redwood supports customer-supplied HSM in the private build. Also we want an audit of data-at-rest encryption.
[04:22] Maya: We have a SOC2 summary (public) and a private packet we can share via secure link. We do support HSM via partner integrations for Private; I'll have Samir include specifics.
[04:33] Samir: I'll attach the KMS rotation note and an architecture diagram. Note some internal terms might be transcribed weirdly — like "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes shows up as "Redwood dedicate" in auto transcripts.
[04:44] Diego: Ha, yes we noticed a few odd transcript bits in last meeting.
[04:48] Maya: Ok let's do a quick timeline recap: Diego to provision VPC peering creds by 9/10, Priya to send required security control list by 9/09, Redwood to run the two bench runs and return results by 9/13, Samir to send KMS/HSM note by 9/09.
[05:04] Aisha: Sounds good. One question — pricing follow-up, any initial estimate if we go to Dedicated?
[05:10] Maya: We can give a ballpark — Dedicated starts to make sense at sustained throughput; we'll send a pricing model tied to throughput and reserved GPU tiers. Exact quote after we validate bench numbers.
[05:20] Liam: Also would be useful to get a small demo of the rollout features (canary/A-B) — to see how to route traffic to fallback models.
[05:28] Samir: We can set up a short ops demo next week — 20 minutes — show canary, rollback, and tracing hooks.
[05:34] Aisha: Please do.
[05:36] Maya: Anything else?
[05:38] Priya: One minor — can you confirm data residency for logs if we run in our EU region?
[05:43] Samir: Yes, region pinning is supported for Private and Dedicated. Hosted API we can pin region for logs depending on contractual controls; we'll include details in the security packet.
[05:53] Diego: I'll follow up with the peering details post-meeting.
[05:56] Maya: Great, thanks all. Recap of next steps in the chat and I'll follow up with the bench sheet + security docs.
[06:05] Aisha: Thanks everyone.
[06:07] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript has occasional imperfect transcriptions (names, product words). Shared artifacts referenced during call: link: https://drive.company/nexa/poc-benchmarks (raw traces), short deck: https://bit.ly/nexa-poc-deck, security packet to be shared via secure Redwood link.
